extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants and institutional staff preparing/submitting SF424 Research & Related applications via ASSIST (SO, PD/PI, AOR, institutional delegates)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing, validating, finalizing, and submitting single- and multi-project SF424 Research & Related grant applications through the NIH ASSIST system, including managing access, components, forms, validations, and post-submission corrections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Format — single-project
rubrics_metrics.description: All electronic single-project applications prepared in ASSIST will include: All required forms necessary for the application package; All optional forms available for the application package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the single-project package contains every required form and include any optional forms that are available for the opportunity; ASSIST will list forms in the component form tabs and can generate a table of contents, headers/footers, and PDFs for preview.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application Format — multi-project (Overall Component & components)
rubrics_metrics.description: All electronic multi-project applications prepared in ASSIST will include: A single Overall Component describing the entire application and how each of the additional components fit together; Other Components (e.g., Admin Core, Project, Core) with predefined data collection requirements set by the agency; Summaries compiled from data provided in individual components (e.g., component and categorical roll-ups of budget data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Overall Component to explain the relationship among components; ensure each agency-defined component type is completed per its data requirements; ASSIST groups components by type and displays numeric identifiers and optional short names for tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use required FORMS package per receipt date
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must use the FORMS application package required for the receipt date (e.g., FORMS-I for receipt dates on or after January 25, 2025; previously FORMS-H for dates on or after January 25, 2023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to High-level Grant Application Form Change Summary and relevant NOT-OD notices (e.g., NOT-OD-24-086, NOT-OD-22-195) for deadlines and details about form changes; use the correct forms package in ASSIST.

rubrics_metrics.name: Browser compatibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Some screens may not display correctly in the Internet Explorer browser with Compatibility Mode turned on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turn off IE Compatibility Mode or use a different browser to ensure screens render correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Login credentials and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST uses the same login authorization service/account as eRA Commons; all ASSIST users must use existing eRA Commons IDs or work through their organization to obtain them. Login.gov is being phased in and may become required; users can access ASSIST via eRA Commons, Login.gov, or InCommon Federated accounts (where supported).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If transitioning to Login.gov, follow the association steps; to access via eRA Commons, log into Commons first and use module navigation or the ASSIST login screen. If using federated login, follow your organization's sign-in process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Login.gov association and two-factor authentication
rubrics_metrics.description: After creating a Login.gov account and associating it with your eRA Commons account, you must use the Login.gov option on the ASSIST home screen and complete the additional authentication method you set up with Login.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may enable 'Remember this browser' to reduce repeated two-factor prompts; ensure your eRA account is active before attempting association; follow troubleshooting steps (clear cache, avoid old bookmarks) if login fails before contacting eRA Service Desk.

rubrics_metrics.name: InCommon Federated account two-factor requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To use an InCommon Federated account to login to Commons your organization must support NIH’s two-factor authentication standards and you must have two-factor authentication setup for your organization’s account.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the organization does not support NIH 2FA or you don't have 2FA enabled, you will not be able to login with InCommon and must use Login.gov; contact your Organization Administrators for org-specific 2FA details; eRA cannot help with the organization's login screens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Password policy and reset process
rubrics_metrics.description: All passwords must follow the NIH eRA Password Policy; if you forget a password or your account is locked, request a reset which generates a temporary password sent to the email on your Commons personal profile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To reset: click Forgot Password/Unlock Account on ASSIST login, enter User ID and email matching Commons profile, submit, then log in with temporary password and choose a new password; expired passwords will prompt a change when accessing ASSIST.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-association password requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: You must not try to associate an InCommon Federated account using a system-assigned temporary eRA password; the eRA account must have a user-chosen password that is not expired or locked before association.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your eRA password is temporary, expired, or the account is locked, change/reset it via Commons first (Forgot Password/Unlock Account) before attempting to associate accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application access control (privileges and access levels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Application access is controlled by assigning appropriate access levels or privileges to system users. An access level is a group of privileges determining view/edit capabilities and scope (entire application vs specific component).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users with an SO role automatically have the Access Maintainer privilege and can assign that privilege to others; manage access carefully to maintain proper edit/view control across components, especially for multi-project applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegations from eRA Commons supported within ASSIST
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST supports delegations from Commons so that multiple users within and outside the applicant organization can be given responsibilities while maintaining access control.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ASSIST Manage Access functions to Add Access for New Users, modify privileges for multi- or single-project applications, and revoke access when necessary; review Manage Access History to audit changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component definition and navigation
rubrics_metrics.description: A component is a named, agency-defined collection of data elements that may be repeated within an application; when Component Information is accessed the included forms for that component are listed across the page in tabs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Navigate forms via component form tabs; components of same type are grouped under a heading and listed with numeric identifiers; optional component short names can be added to help track components.

rubrics_metrics.name: Component status requirements for multi-project submission
rubrics_metrics.description: To prepare a multi-project application for submission: verify at least one component is in Final status and that other components are in either Final or Abandoned status; verify that the status of the application is All Components Final; perform validations so status becomes All Components Validated; update to Ready for Submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the specific step sequence: Finalize components, validate the application, then update submission status before submitting; components not Final/Abandoned will block submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application validation (system and business rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST can run validations on federal-wide and agency business rules prior to submission. Applications can only be updated to Ready for Submission status when they have passed all system and business validations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Validate Application button to run application-level or individual component validations; review Errors and Warnings Results; errors must be corrected before submission, warnings may permit submission but should be reviewed and corrected as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validation types: field, format, required field
rubrics_metrics.description: Form and field level validations include Field Data Format Validations and Required Field Validations which detect missing or improperly formatted data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address field-level validation messages on the indicated form and component; some validations occur on status update actions (e.g., when changing to Ready for Submission ASSIST performs validations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission authorization and AOR credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a Signing Official for the Applicant Lead Organization, who is an Authorized Organizational Representative (AOR), can submit the application. ASSIST prompts for Grants.gov AOR credentials when submitting (these are Grants.gov credentials, not ASSIST or eRA Commons credentials).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Have AOR Grants.gov username/password ready when clicking Submit Application; entering these passes the application to Grants.gov and updates ASSIST submission status to Submitted with recorded dates/times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission 2-business-day application viewing window
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting, you have a 2 business day application viewing window to check your assembled application. Your application automatically moves forward to receipt and referral staff after the viewing window has elapsed unless you explicitly 'reject' the application in eRA Commons Status module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submitted an administrative supplement, a signing official can skip the two-day window by clicking Verify in the Commons Status module; use the viewing window to check assembled e-application PDF images and correct issues if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-submission errors and warnings handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When an application is submitted, the offering agency performs validations; if errors exist the application is put into Submission Errors and Agency errors/warnings are viewable. Errors must be corrected before resubmitting; warnings may allow resubmission but should be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: View Grants.gov and Agency Submission Errors/Warnings via links in the submission status details; Agency Errors and Warnings Results page shows Component ID & Title, Form Name, and Error/Warning Message with guidance for resolving issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revise a submitted application procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST users with authority to edit an entire application may revise an application after submission by updating the application status to Work in Progress and updating component(s) to Work in Progress before making edits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Steps: Update Submission Status to Work in Progress (optionally add comment), select component, Update Component Status to Work in Progress (add comments), then edit the necessary forms and resubmit following validation and submission steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restore previous version / PO edits refresh rules
rubrics_metrics.description: If a program official edits an application in HSS, the application must be refreshed in ASSIST to view the edits. Refreshing an application that is in Work in Progress status will overwrite any unsubmitted updates with the version available to federal agency staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only use Restore Previous Version when instructed (PO will email SO/PI); in Actions click Restore Previous Version and Continue to refresh; be aware that local unsubmitted changes will be lost.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person Profile eRA Commons ID requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: All personnel listed on the R&R Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) Form must have an eRA Commons ID. NIH grant applicants will receive an error if the 'Credential, e.g., agency field' is blank or does not contain a valid eRA Commons ID for all personnel on the form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This includes Senior/Key Personnel and Other Significant Contributors; correct errors before submission; see NOT-OD-24-042 and Nexus article for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify Senior/Key Personnel matching and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST identifies potentially matched persons and determines matches for Senior/Key Personnel; when finalizing component biosketches you must select which biosketch to include in the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When finalizing a component, select the biosketch (current component or previously finalized component) via radio button and click Submit Biosketches; use Cancel Status Change to cancel without saving; the unselected biosketch is removed from the Senior/Key Personnel form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants.gov and Agency tracking and status fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Application Information and ASSIST Status details should display fields such as Application Identifier, Opportunity Number, Project Title, PD/PI Name, Organization, Grants.gov Tracking #, Last Status Check, Submission Date, Submitting AOR, ASSIST Submission Status, and Submission Status Date. Grants.gov and Agency statuses include tracking numbers, received dates, processing status, and links for submission errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the View Submission Status Details link to inspect ASSIST, Grants.gov, and Agency statuses and to access View Grants.gov Submission Errors or View Agency Submission Errors and Warnings if present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generating and previewing application images
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST can generate a preview of the entire application, generate and view the initial application image, view previously generated images, request a new application image, preview a component or form, and preview the current form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use preview functionality to check assembled PDFs and images prior to and during the post-submission viewing window; request new images if changes have been made and need to be rechecked.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachments management
rubrics_metrics.description: Users must manage attachments appropriately with the ability to Add Attachment, Replace Attachment, Delete Attachment, and View Attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow ASSIST attachment workflows for each form; when replacing or deleting attachments be mindful of component finalization and which attachments are selected to be included in the final application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional forms addition
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST allows adding Optional Forms for both single-project and multi-project applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the Add Optional Forms functionality to include opportunity-specific optional forms; optional forms for multi-project applications may differ from single-project ones—check the component-level optional forms list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects & Clinical Trials Study Record structure
rubrics_metrics.description: The Study Record consists of multiple sections: Section 1 Basic Information; Section 2 Study Population Characteristics (including Inclusion Enrollment Report); Section 3 Protection and Monitoring Plans; Section 4 Protocol Synopsis; Section 5 Other Clinical Trial-Related Attachments; Section 6 Clinical Milestone Plan.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete each Study Record section as required; participant-level data collection, export/upload to ClinicalTrials.gov, and XML export/upload features are supported—check uploaded data on ClinicalTrials.gov after submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant-level data collection and ClinicalTrials.gov uploads
rubrics_metrics.description: ASSIST supports exporting and uploading participant-level data to ClinicalTrials.gov, uploading human subjects data directly, checking uploaded data, and exporting human subjects data to an XML file for upload.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the provided steps to export/upload and verify data on ClinicalTrials.gov; ensure study record and participant-level data meet ClinicalTrials.gov requirements prior to upload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Errors and Warnings Results content expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agency Errors and Warnings Results page shows errors and warnings detected during processing by the grantor Agency and includes fields for Component ID & Title (multi-project), Form Name, and Error Message or Warning Message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors must be corrected before re-submitting; error messages include guidance for resolving the issue; warnings provide explanations and should be reviewed even if submission is allowed with warnings.
